passages.title: Dialogue 1: The new office
passages.text:
Man: So, what do you think of the new office, now we've been here a week?
Woman: I was worried it'd be really noisy with everyone in one big room, but actually it's been fine. And because the design team sit right next to us now, I can just turn round and ask them things instead of sending emails. We've sorted out more problems this week than in the whole of last month.
Man: The journey's worse for me, though. It's a much longer walk from the station.
Woman: Oh, it's about the same for me.

passages.title: Dialogue 2: The café job
passages.text:
Girl: I heard you're giving up your job at the café. Is it the money?
Boy: No, the pay's actually quite good for a weekend job, and Sue, the manager, is lovely. It's just that my exams start in May, and at the moment I'm working every Saturday and Sunday. I've got so much revision to do that something has to go.
Girl: Will they let you come back in the summer?
Boy: Sue says they will, so that's good.

passages.title: Dialogue 3: An online language course
passages.text:
Woman: How's your online Spanish course going?
Man: Well, I'm not sure about the teacher. She talks really fast and she doesn't always explain the grammar.
Woman: I've found that with mine too. But for thirty pounds a term, you can't really complain, can you? The evening class at the college costs four times that.
Man: That's true. You get a lot for the price. And the lessons are only forty minutes, which suits me.
Woman: Me too. I couldn't concentrate for any longer after work.

passages.title: Dialogue 4: A word with the manager
passages.text:
Woman: Have you got a minute, Mr Clarke?
Man: Of course, Helen. If it's about your holiday dates, I've already said yes.
Woman: Thanks, but it's not that. I heard that Tom's team is behind with the new website. I've finished all my own work for this month, so I wondered if I could join them for a couple of weeks.
Man: That would be a big help, actually. Tom will be delighted.

passages.title: Dialogue 5: A job interview
passages.text:
Boy: How was the interview for the summer job at the museum?
Girl: They kept me waiting for twenty minutes, which wasn't ideal, but I didn't really mind because it gave me time to calm down. And then it went better than I expected. I'd read all about the museum beforehand, so I could answer all their questions, and they even laughed at my joke about the dinosaurs!
Boy: It sounds like you'll get it.
Girl: Well, I really think I've got a good chance.

passages.title: Dialogue 6: Starting university
passages.text:
Woman: So you've started your engineering course. What's it like?
Man: It's hard work. The lectures are long, but the lecturers make them really interesting. What I love most, though, is the time in the workshop. Last week we built a small bridge and tested how much weight it could take. That's why I chose engineering, really.
Woman: And it's four years, isn't it? That seems a long time.
Man: It goes quickly when you enjoy it.

questions.question: You will hear two colleagues talking about their new office. What does the woman think about it?
options: a) It is too noisy with everyone in one big room.
b) It makes it easier to share information.
c) It takes her longer to get there.
questions.explanation: The woman says she can 'just turn round and ask' the design team instead of sending emails, and they have 'sorted out more problems'. She expected noise but says 'actually it's been fine', and it is the man, not the woman, who has a longer journey; for her it is 'about the same'.

questions.question: You will hear two students talking about a part-time job. Why is the boy leaving his job at the café?
options: b) He doesn't get on with his manager.
c) He needs more time to study.
questions.explanation: The boy says his exams start in May and 'I've got so much revision to do that something has to go'. He says the pay is 'quite good' and the manager 'is lovely', so the other reasons are wrong.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about online language courses. What do they agree about?
options: a) The courses are good value for money.
b) The lessons are too long to follow after work.
c) The teachers explain things clearly.
questions.explanation: The woman says 'for thirty pounds a term, you can't really complain' and the man agrees: 'That's true. You get a lot for the price.' They both like the forty-minute lessons, so they do not think they are too long, and both say their teachers do not always explain things well.

questions.question: You will hear a woman talking to her manager. Why has she come to see him?
options: a) To offer to help with some work
b) To ask for some time off
c) To complain about a colleague
questions.explanation: Helen has finished her own work and asks 'if I could join them for a couple of weeks' to help Tom's team with the website. She says 'it's not that' when the manager mentions her holiday, and she mentions that Tom's team is behind only to explain her offer, not to complain.

questions.question: You will hear a girl talking about a job interview. How does she feel about it?
options: a) Worried that she wasn't prepared
b) Pleased with how she did
c) Annoyed that it started late
questions.explanation: The girl says 'it went better than I expected' and 'I really think I've got a good chance'. She was kept waiting but 'didn't really mind', and she had prepared well: 'I'd read all about the museum beforehand'.

questions.question: You will hear a man talking about his university course. What is his opinion of it?
options: b) Four years is too long for a course like this.
c) The practical work is the best part.
questions.explanation: The man says that what he loves most is "the time in the workshop", where they build and test things, so the practical work is the best part for him. He does not find the lectures boring, because he says the lecturers make them interesting, and he does not think four years is too long: he says the time goes quickly when you enjoy it.
